title: Legal charges complicate the profit slowdown
question: How should readers interpret the reported profit slowdown alongside the disclosed legal charges?
comparability_limits: The two GAAP-income series compare the same three-month quarters year over year. The charge series contains only the specifically disclosed current-year charges; it does not claim that prior-year legal charges were zero.
The Q2 release also discloses $1.18 billion of severance expenses. Adding back only the plotted legal charge would not create a consistently normalized earnings series across these quarters.

The Q3 company's charge-excluded illustration is $22.88 billion, rounded in the source. Exact reported operating income of $12.988 billion plus the $9.890 billion charge yields $22.878 billion before rounding. Neither number is a measure of recurring profit or AI return.
A GAAP expense recognized in a quarter is not evidence that the same amount was paid in cash in that quarter. No legal-payment cash adjustment is made to operating cash flow or free cash flow.
The 2025 Q3 effective tax rate was 87%, versus 24% in Q3 2026. The net-income/EPS growth comparison is therefore not interchangeable with the operating-income comparison shown here.

Legal obligations remain an economic cost. The company has an interest in emphasizing charge-excluded results; do not use its illustration as independent proof of underlying profitability or investment success.
